title: AI Factory Swarm customer spec (tests as data)
description: One file under `.migration/spec/<slice>/`, ADR-0061. A capability's behaviour as data: cases that act through a public entry point (an HTTP request or a management command) and say what must come back, in the domain's words. `afs-spec` runs them; no case names a module, class or function of the code.

capability.description: The ledger entry (`.migration/ledger/<capability>.yaml`) whose rules these cases prove.

background.description: Setup every case starts from, before its own `given`.

title.description: What the case shows, in the domain's words.

rule.description: The ledger rule id (or ids) this case proves.

oracle.description: Where the expected values come from: a recorded legacy output or characterization test, as a path from the repo root (ADR-0062). The legacy app is the independent oracle; a value from anywhere else needs a `ruling`. With the profile's `spec.required`, every case names an oracle or a ruling, and the path must exist.

ruling.description: The quirk ruling an expected value comes from, when it differs from what the legacy app did (ADR-0061: a spec never silently keeps a legacy bug).

examples.description: Table form: one case per row; `{column}` in given, when and then is replaced by the row's value.

forall.description: Property form (ADR-0069): `{name}` in given, when and then takes values from these ranges; the case must hold for every one. Not with `examples`.

fixtures.description: Data fixtures the stack loads first (Django: `loaddata` paths). A fixture is part of the spec: it lives under `.migration/spec/` and exists when the spec is checked (ADR-0078). Prefer `requests`, which don't depend on the target's schema.

commands.description: Side-channel setup commands, run before the action.

requests.description: ADR-0078: requests through the public HTTP interface that set up the case's starting state, sent in order after fixtures and commands. Each must succeed (a status below 400), or the case fails. This is how a spec written before the code sets up state without naming the target's schema.

clock.description: Today's date (and time) as the code sees it: a boundary, so it may be set. Or `{column}`, taken from the case's examples.

gateways.description: ADR-0068: a real local HTTP stub per named gateway (the profile's spec.gateways says how the target finds it), answering in order; the last answer repeats.

respond.description: An answer, or a list of answers in order.

unreachable.description: Point the target at a port nothing listens on.

when.description: Exactly one action, through a public entry point.

htmx.description: Send it as an htmx request (`HX-Request: true`).

replay.description: Replay one recorded legacy exchange (ADR-0067): its request is sent to the target, and `then.replay` compares the response with the recorded one. The recording is the oracle.

recording.description: A JSON file of exchanges, from the repo root: {name: {request: {method, path, form?, json?, headers?}, response: {status, body, content_type?}}}.

exchange.description: The exchange's name in that file; may be `{column}` from the examples.

under.description: The key the exchanges sit under, when the recording nests them (e.g. `responses`).

then.description: What must come back. At least one assertion: a case can't be empty.

oneOf.description: `{column}`: the row's value, with its own type

status.description: HTTP status, or a command's exit status (0 ok, 1 it raised).

json.description: The JSON body must contain this (objects match on the keys given; lists and values match exactly).

text.description: Each must appear in the body or output.

replay.description: With `when.replay`: the status must be the recorded one, and the body must match it after normalizing.

body.description: exact: the body, line endings and trailing spaces normalized; text: the visible text (tags dropped, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed); json: equal as JSON; ignore: only the status.

mask.description: Regular expressions replaced by <masked> on both sides: values that differ by design (dates, ids, tokens).

sent.description: ADR-0068: exactly the requests each stubbed gateway received, in order (method and path equal, body containing the text given). [] means none.

schema.description: ADR-0068: the JSON body must satisfy this JSON Schema: inline, or a file from the repo root. The contract of an API whose values can't be fixed.

number.description: A number taken from the body (the pattern's first group, or the whole match) must be within bounds: how a property states an invariant.

oneOf.description: `{column}`: the row's value, with its own type

generator.description: A range or a list a property case draws from (ADR-0069).
